author: chancez
body:
**What is this feature?**

Enables visually hightlighting an area on the flamegraph and zooming into it. The existing behavior of clicking on an individual node is still available.

**Why do we need this feature?**

This differs from the current zoom because it allows zooming across multiple nodes, rather than into a single node and it's children.

This is useful because some smaller nodes in a flamegraph do not have a parent which can be zoomed (the root node) or, zooming to the parent doesn't provide enough of a zoom, due to other siblings taking a larger portion of the level.

**Who is this feature for?**

When viewing a flamegraph, if one node is too big, or certain nodes are simply too small, relative to their siblings, they aren't visible, and it's difficult to view what their contents are. Being able to visually select an area on the graph to zoom allows you to zoom into these areas incrementally.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes #58373

**Special notes for your reviewer**: 

My usage of `useRef` on the selection and `setSelection` is probably suspect. I'm new to react and I found the selection values were not being updated immediately when calling `setSelection`. It is my understanding that stateful values are lazily updated after useEffect runs. Since I need to track the value of startX and endX in the event handlers to compare them, I need the values to be immediately available. To fix this  I used `setSelection` with a reference to work around it. This solution basically came straight from stackoverflow, so I'm not sure if there is a better way.

author: calda
body:
This PR fixes an issue where an empty trim item would take precedence over a non-empty trim item. Fixes #1841.

In this case, the circle layers have two trims:
 1. A trim with no keyframes, displaying 0% to 100% of the path the entire time. This item is a no-op since it doesn't affect how the path is rendered.
 2. A trim that actually animates

Since we we use `items.first(Trim.self)` here, we were using the first no-op trim item rather than the second one that we actually want. As a fix we can just ignore the first one since it's a no-op anyway.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

Note that two of the JSON files are not valid JSON as per the RFC since they are not valid UTF-8. When that happens, we simply grab a raw string (effectively just pointing inside the input document). author: dwelle
body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/5926

Turned out way more complex than anticipated, and this rewrite is still somewhat error-prone:

- since ContextMenu is now in the component tree, its items are re-evaluated on each rerender (while contextMenu is open). This means the item's `contextMenuPredicate()` (or `perform()` when executed) may throw if the state changed between open and render/confirm. This can happen if the user makes an action that doesn't close the contextMenu but changes selection (or other state the action works on).
  
  Current workaround:
  
  - filter out items based on their predicates on render, not state update (when `contextMenu.items` is populated)
  - close the contextMenu before selection is deselected on `pointerDown`
  
  What we should do instead:
  
  - [ ] make contextMenu (meaning Actions) operate on the state it was opened on, not on current state

- closing contextMenu is prone to race conditions. E.g., the contextMenu action user clicks on can update appState using the appState it's being passed, which still contains open `appState.contextMenu`.
  
  Current workaround:
  
  - wait until contextMenu is closed before executing contextMenu items
  
  What we should do instead:
  
  - Honestly, don't know. We can stop requiring actions to return fully qualified `appState` (by moving to latest TS and enabling [exactOptionalPropertyTypes](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#exactOptionalPropertyTypes), but that won't enforce correct behavior). We can also ensure we reset the `contextMenu` on the `appState` that we pass to actions (but that will require support for passing custom `appState` when executing an action, as opposed to leaving it up to the manager. But if we do the previous suggestion of making contextMenu actions operate on initial state, then this will need to be done anyway).

- it also uncovers the issue of not having an easy way to subscribe on change to state/elements that should close the contextMenu, such as changing tools.

Alas, it will have to do for now and we'll improve it as we continue rewriting the editor flow.

----

- In this PR, we're now evaluating `contextItemPredicate` in place (render) instead of when setting the items, which simplifies things (and also fixes some things as per above).
- Separators are deduplicated instead of inlining the checks for it on open.
- Fixed the "right-clicking on common bounding box" doesn't open contextMenu as `element` type.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
[XLA] Make HloModuleConfig own the string keys in `analysis_allowance_map_`

This fixes a use-after-free bug when deserializing an HloModuleConfig:
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/f1251be0983f36616bcf6d3fa896d01dcbf82fdb/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/hlo_module_config.cc#L304-L306

Without this change, the keys of `analysis_allowance_map_` have the
same lifetime as the input proto that's being deserialized, which is
probably very inconvenient semantics for the caller. In practice there
are not many keys and they're short, so I don't think the extra string
copy will have a noticeable performance impact.

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/compare/v1.12.4...v1.12.5)

## Summary of Changes

**Minor Changes:**

-   bpf: Implement downgrading path from v3 to v2 backend map ([#​22416](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22416), [@​YutaroHayakawa](https://togithub.com/YutaroHayakawa))

**Bugfixes:**

-   Clear stale CNP status nodes if updates have been disabled (Backport PR [#​22500](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22500), Upstream PR [#​20366](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/20366), [@​pippolo84](https://togithub.com/pippolo84))
-   docs: Update Cilium Sphinx RTD Theme reference (Backport PR [#​22500](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22500), Upstream PR [#​22321](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22321), [@​kimstacy](https://togithub.com/kimstacy))
-   Fail validate-cnp preflight check if a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy is using an empty toEndpoints/fromEndpoints selector (Backport PR [#​22500](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22500), Upstream PR [#​21990](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/21990), [@​thorn3r](https://togithub.com/thorn3r))
-   Fix bug that could lead to inconsistent pod IP information between agents, sometimes leading to a failure to decrypt IPsec traffic. (Backport PR [#​22308](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22308), Upstream PR [#​22127](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22127), [@​aanm](https://togithub.com/aanm))
-   Fix bug where configuring the API rate limiter options could fail when providing multiple options (Backport PR [#​22696](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22696), Upstream PR [#​22299](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22299), [@​thorn3r](https://togithub.com/thorn3r))
-   Fix Cilium fatal "Could not create or update CiliumNode resource, despite retries" on environments with `enable-ipv4-egress-gateway` (Backport PR [#​22308](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22308), Upstream PR [#​22298](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22298), [@​aanm](https://togithub.com/aanm))
-   Fix forwarding of the security identity by the DNS proxy which could cause random policy denials (Backport PR [#​22407](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22407), Upstream PR [#​22361](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22361), [@​aspsk](https://togithub.com/aspsk))
-   Fix GC of CEPs that were not GCed by kube-apiserver (Backport PR [#​22308](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22308), Upstream PR [#​22213](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22213), [@​aanm](https://togithub.com/aanm))
-   fix: some tofqdn flags not being parsed (Backport PR [#​22500](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22500), Upstream PR [#​22346](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22346), [@​carloscastrojumo](https://togithub.com/carloscastrojumo))
-   helm: Add relabelings config to ServiceMonitors and re-introduce node label on cilium/hubble metrics (Backport PR [#​22506](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22506), Upstream PR [#​22297](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22297), [@​chancez](https://togithub.com/chancez))
-   Improve garbage collection for FQDNs particularly with high-churn IP names such as Amazon S3. (Backport PR [#​22730](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22730), Upstream PR [#​22510](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22510), [@​joestringer](https://togithub.com/joestringer))
-   Prevent cilium operator crash in AWS region with IPv6-only ENIs without subnet filters. (Backport PR [#​22308](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22308), Upstream PR [#​22075](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22075), [@​bimmlerd](https://togithub.com/bimmlerd))

**CI Changes:**

-   .github: Explicitly set build-commits job runner image version and install libtinfo5 (Backport PR [#​22328](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22328), Upstream PR [#​22315](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22315), [@​chancez](https://togithub.com/chancez))
-   .github: fix bpf-checks on ubuntu-latest runner (Backport PR [#​22328](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22328), Upstream PR [#​22322](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22322), [@​julianwiedmann](https://togithub.com/julianwiedmann))
-   Fix CODEOWNERS ([#​22292](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22292), [@​michi-covalent](https://togithub.com/michi-covalent))

**Misc Changes:**

-   .github/workflows: split the image tag update in two steps (Backport PR [#​22260](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22260), Upstream PR [#​22268](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22268), [@​aanm](https://togithub.com/aanm))
-   Add automatic creation of Cilium base images (Backport PR [#​22260](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22260), Upstream PR [#​22179](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22179), [@​aanm](https://togithub.com/aanm))
-   bpf: Remove FIB lookup for IPsec (Backport PR [#​22308](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22308), Upstream PR [#​22069](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22069), [@​pchaigno](https://togithub.com/pchaigno))
-   build(deps): bump actions/setup-go from 3.3.1 to 3.4.0 ([#​22486](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22486), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump actions/setup-go from 3.4.0 to 3.5.0 ([#​22715](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22715), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump actions/upload-artifact from 3.1.0 to 3.1.1 ([#​22271](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22271), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump github/codeql-action from 2.1.32 to 2.1.35 ([#​22497](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22497), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump github/codeql-action from 2.1.35 to 2.1.36 ([#​22632](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22632), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump helm/kind-action from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0 ([#​22716](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22716), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   build(deps): bump KyleMayes/install-llvm-action from 1.6.0 to 1.6.1 ([#​22595](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22595), [@​dependabot](https://togithub.com/dependabot)\[bot])
-   chore(deps): update base-images (v1.12) ([#​22167](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22167), [@​renovate](https://togithub.com/renovate)\[bot])
-   chore(deps): update docker.io/library/golang:1.18.8 docker digest to [`0936e74`](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/commit/0936e74) (v1.12) ([#​22198](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/22198), [@​renovate](https://togithub.com/renovate)\[bot])

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: dfrg
body:
This adds a new crate called `punchcut` containing the initial TrueType glyph scaling code based on `read-fonts`. The caching and hinting code has been extracted to hopefully make this more reviewable.

A few notes:
* There are fixed point math functions that have some overlap with code in `font-types`. FreeType provides outline points as either integral font units or fixed point (26.6) values depending on whether a scale has been applied. We copy that here and that makes some of the math and types less than ideal. I'm open to options for making this nicer (without loss in perf/memory) but I'd like to not block the initial cut on it.
* There is a tiered architecture that exposes the individual sources (just `glyf` for now) as well as a higher level interface at the root of the crate. The layering feels pretty good to me right now, but comments for improvement are welcome.
* I've tried to comment some of the bits in `source/glyf/scaler.rs` that might be tricky. Feel free to point out any that require further explanation.

This has nice integration with `kurbo`: the `Outline` type implements `kurbo::Shape` so these can be fed directly into `vello` (née piet-gpu). I plan on using this for glyph loading support in that crate soon™.

### Motivation and Context

`./scripts/zloop/sh` is reliably failing in the master branch.

### Description

This reverts commit d30db519af44b905fc52b8c8ba34f6378aa03470.  With this change applied zloop.sh fails reliably with the following ASSERT.

```
  zio_wait(zio_claim(NULL, zcb->zcb_spa, refcnt ? 0 : spa_min_claim_txg(zcb->zcb_spa), bp, NULL, NULL, ZIO_FLAG_CANFAIL)) == 0 (0x2 == 0x0)
  ASSERT at cmd/zdb/zdb.c:5452:zdb_count_block()
```

### How Has This Been Tested?

Locally confirmed that after reverting this change `zloop.sh` no longer fails in `zdb` consistently.
